blocks: Methodology Note for Transparency International
October 2025
Background
■​ Data provided by InfluenceMap for this report is sourced from LobbyMap, the world’s first and leading

platform to track and score companies and their industry associations on their climate policy engagement and influence. Covering over 1,000 companies and 330 industry associations worldwide, the independent assessments enable investors and other stakeholders to distinguish between companies that are genuinely transition-ready and those that may be engaging in greenwashing.
■​ InfluenceMap defines “policy engagement” using the UN Guide for Responsible Corporate Engagement
in Climate Policy (2013), which defines a range of corporate activities as engagement, such as advertising, social media, public relations, and direct contact with regulators and elected officials.
■​ Using this definition, the LobbyMap process collects evidence from a range of publicly accessible data

sources to build a reliable representation of corporate policy engagement. These include organizational websites, senior management statements, regulatory consultation comments, financial disclosures, and reports from reliable media outlets.
■​ The methodology is designed to be “policy neutral,” and InfluenceMap does not take internal positions

on the best climate policy. Instead, the scoring system measures corporate positions against external, authoritative benchmarks. These are derived from IPCC science (science-based policy benchmarks), as well as statements and proposals from government-mandated bodies tasked with delivering on the
Paris Agreement’s goals.
Read more about the LobbyMap methodology.
Methodology for the ‘COP30 trends’ database
■​ The dataset covers the 466 companies and industry associations in the LobbyMap database that
attended COP28 and/or COP29.
■​ Scores for corporate engagement on COP30 priority policy issues since the start of 2024 have been
extracted from LobbyMap using keyword searches to reveal how companies and industry associations that attended COP28 and/or COP29 have been engaging on key policy areas in national and regional

regulatory contexts. Identified evidence since the start of 2024 was aggregated to provide an indication of overall position and engagement level for each entity. This illustrates what policy engagement could entail at COP30.
■​ The key policy areas isolated were: (1) Paris Agreement; (2) Response to Climate Science; (3) Nationally
Determined Contributions; (4) Energy Transition; (5) Deforestation and Land Use
